problem: Goal-oriented VLN agents are pretrained almost exclusively by imitating shortest-path trajectories (with instruction augmentation), so they lack exploration priors and generalize poorly to unseen environments; human exploration demonstrations are too costly to scale.
motivation: Goal-oriented instructions describe only the target, so agents must explore rooms, tell similar rooms apart and correct mistakes. Exploration demonstrations are missing at scale, and RL is unstable and expensive. The observation is that a trained agent's own successful (non-shortest) rollouts are exploratory and can serve as better demonstrations than shortest paths.
key_idea: Iteratively train a DUET agent on image-goal navigation, keep only its own successful exploration rollouts as demonstrations for the next round, scale this to 860 environments, then convert the trajectories into language-goal data with VLM captions for goal-oriented VLN pretraining.
insight: Gains come from the agent's own exploration paths, not from random paths or extra data. Random trajectories of similar length only match shortest-path performance (Table random_ablate), and adding shortest paths in HM3D helps less than explored paths (REVERIE SR 55.16 vs 59.39). The self-demonstrations explore more rooms (4.21 vs 2.77 rooms), and pretraining on them also helps when finetuning on shortest paths.
method: Base data D0: shortest paths of 5-7 viewpoints between MP3D viewpoint pairs (~181k paths, ~6.5M visual-goal trajectories using the 36 panorama images as goals).
Base agent: DUET trained on D0 (pretraining with SAP, then finetuning) with a single-action-prediction loss.
Rollout curation: the agent rolls out from the start viewpoint toward the visual goal; only trajectories that reach the correct target within the path-length limit are kept as D_t.

Iterative self-improvement: each round retrains a fresh agent from scratch on D_{t-1} (pretrain and finetune) to avoid inheriting low-quality data; finetuning interleaves teacher forcing on demonstrations with student forcing supervised by shortest-path oracle actions; sampling is 75% on-trajectory points and 25% hard negatives.
Scaling: after 3 MP3D rounds, add 800 HM3D environments and run one more round, giving 860 environments and ~60M visual-goal trajectories.

VLM caption transfer: InternVL-26B writes detailed captions for 18 of 36 panorama images at each goal; captions replace images, producing 46.5M language-goal exploration trajectories (SID-46M); detail-style captions beat REVERIE/SOON-style ones.
Downstream: pretrain DUET with SAP+MLM on SID-46M, finetune on REVERIE/SOON/ObjectNav; also convert trajectories to continuous form to augment StreamVLN for VLN-CE.

setting.backbone: DUET (dual-scale graph transformer, LXMERT init, DINOv2+SigLIP vision encoders), trained from scratch; StreamVLN (LLaVA-Video 7B) for VLN-CE; InternVL-26B for captioning
setting.model_size: StreamVLN 7B; InternVL 26B (captioner); DUET size not stated
setting.training_data: Self-generated image-goal exploration trajectories on 860 MP3D+HM3D environments (SID-46M language-goal, 46.5M) plus downstream REVERIE/SOON data; VLN-CE adds R2R-CE, EnvDrop and ScaleVLN data
setting.observation: panoramic RGB (36 views) plus object features on a topological graph; RGB-D egocentric for VLN-CE (StreamVLN)
setting.action_space: discrete nav-graph viewpoints (VLN-CE: low-level forward 0.25 m / turn 15°)

results: SID sets new state of the art on SOON (val-unseen SR 50.9 vs 44.7 for Meta-Explore; test-unseen SR 47.7 vs 40.5 for GOAT) and REVERIE (val-unseen SR 59.4, SPL 46.0, vs ScaleVLN* 58.4/43.5). It also improves transferred ObjectNav (SR 76 vs DUET 68) and VLN-CE (StreamVLN SR 52.8→53.9, with a slight SPL drop).
limitations: Exploration can fail in complex scenes with many choices, hitting the step limit; transfer to VLN depends on VLM captions that may hallucinate.
Agent is trained under discrete robotic navigation assumptions; embodiment and sim-to-real gaps remain, and no real-robot test.
Large compute cost (about 5,000 GPU hours in total on A800), and the VLN-CE gain is small with lower SPL.
